title: Reward Model Overoptimization: Length Bias as a Controlled Variable

original_idea.problem: The degree to which PPO training exploits length bias vs. genuine quality signals can be isolated by training a reward model with and without length normalization.
original_idea.direction: Train two reward models on the same preference dataset: one standard, one with explicit length normalization. Run PPO fine-tuning against each. Evaluate gold-quality, response length, reward score, and quality degradation.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: isolating length bias contribution to overoptimization gives a clean, reproducible baseline for understanding proxy reward failure modes. This directly informs reward model design choices with clear safety implications for RLHF deployment.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires training two reward models, implementing length normalization, running PPO training twice, and setting up gold evaluation. The RL pipeline (reward model training + PPO) is complex and error-prone. Beginners would struggle significantly with this multi-stage ML pipeline.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Multiple stages: train reward models, run PPO, evaluate. While conceptually clean, the implementation has many moving parts. First meaningful deliverable (comparing reward model scores) is reachable, but the full PPO comparison likely exceeds 30hrs for a beginner.

novelty.reasoning: 'Adaptive Length Bias Mitigation in Reward Models for RLHF' (NAACL Findings 2025) directly addresses this by decomposing reward into length and quality components and implementing length normalization. Multiple 2024-2025 papers characterize length bias in reward models and propose mitigation strategies. The specific experiment of training two reward models (with/without length normalization) and running PPO against each is closely mirrored by existing work. The remaining contribution would be a very clean controlled comparison at small scale, but the research question is substantially answered.
